perf_validation.approach: Path B — platform-only: compute total + uniqExact(ocr) per month from clarity.hits_hot/hits_cold instead of adding a chlocal-owned uniq-state pre-aggregate.
perf_validation.measurement: Read-only, production ClickHouse Cloud, driver-run. Query shape: SELECT toStartOfMonth(hit_created_at), hit_type, count(), uniqExact(ocr) FROM clarity.hits_cold FINAL WHERE _peerdb_is_deleted=0 [AND <org_col>=<id>] AND hit_created_at >= 13-month window GROUP BY month, hit_type. Wall clock: 0.27s scoped by hotlist_org_id to the largest org (14.1M of 24.96M rows); 0.33s scoped by kit_org_id (column absent from the sort key); 0.37s UNSCOPED across all orgs. Table sizes: hits_cold 24,961,523; hits_hot 2,795,122; hit_stats_daily 218,538; zod.public_hits 308,664,520.
perf_validation.note: Refutes the fast pass's blocker: the 308M figure is zod.public_hits (the Postgres CDC mirror), NOT the table a dedup query reads. The operative table is ~25M rows and the full 13-month grouped uniqExact is sub-second even unscoped, so no chlocal schema change is required on performance grounds.

Test approach deviated from the suggested DB::listen query-count assertion: the insight-lpr/laravel-clickhouse-eloquent driver never fires Laravel's QueryExecuted event (proved via tinker), so DB::listen would have silently counted 0 regardless of real query volume — a false green. Likewise a timing-based 'CH down' assertion was replaced with a deterministic restore-then-check, because 127.0.0.1:1 returns instant ECONNREFUSED rather than timing out.

Tile help text, iterated three times on operator feedback. Final (62 chars): 'Hits, counted once per plate. The total below counts every hit.' The key correction was FRAMING: both numbers count hits, one deduped by plate — earlier drafts implied two different metrics and used the ambiguous phrase 'the smaller number' (the headline is the numerically smaller value, so it read backwards). Guarded by tests: both behaviours asserted, 'smaller number' banned, and ScanCount keeps the generic default.

Post-close best-practices review (3 findings) fixed. (1) CROSS-DATABASE MISMATCH: HitStatsBatchQuery hardcoded 'clarity.' while HitPlateStatsBatchQuery used clarityDb(), so under any env where CLICKHOUSE_DATABASE_CLARITY != 'clarity' (the standard per-worktree local-CH QA setup) one tile read its two numbers from two different databases — demonstrated with the connection set to clarity_some_worktree. Fixed by making the sibling resolve via clarityDb() too (prod unaffected: it resolves to literal 'clarity'). (2) TEST ISOLATION: 6 dead-port injections vs 3 restores and no tearDown; added a tearDown() so restore is unconditional. (3) IMPLICIT COUPLING: cache-key prefixes derived from class_basename(static::class) had to coincidentally match a $hitWidgetMap key or the guards silently never fire and every render re-queries; replaced all three sites with hitWidgetPrefix(), which resolves from the authoritative map via getHitStatsColumn() and throws LogicException if a widget is unmapped. Dropped the now-unused Str import. Tests: HitStatsBatchQueryTest 2 (regression on the modified sibling), 30 filtered, 86 dashboard widgets, 217 pages — all green.

Operator-requested de-duplication after the review fixes. (1) Extracted collectUncachedMonths() in SharedHitStatsData — the 18-line 13-month uncached-scan loop was byte-identical in resolvePastMonths() and resolvePastUniqueMonths() apart from the namespace; one copy now guarantees both series ask about the SAME months. (2) Within EACH query class (not across them — they query different tables with different aggregates and org/date columns, so nothing is shareable between them), extracted aggregates(), fromAndWhere(), toCounts() and zeroCounts(), which handle() and handleRange() previously duplicated verbatim. DELIBERATELY NOT merged: the resolver pairs themselves — measured 51 and 63 differing lines, because the unique path carries the negative-cache marker, the null-on-failure contract and the direct handle() call; collapsing them behind flags would be less readable than the duplication. Tests: 32 filtered, 86 dashboard widgets, 217 pages, all green.

Operator pushback: toCounts()/zeroCounts() were unnecessary. Correct — wrapping a four-key array literal in a named private static method adds indirection without preventing anything, and the earlier de-duplication pass over-corrected. Both helpers removed from BOTH query classes and the array literals inlined at their 3 call sites each. KEPT: aggregates() and fromAndWhere(), which prevent real SQL drift between handle() and handleRange() (the class of bug the review already caught once with the hardcoded clarity. prefix), and collectUncachedMonths(), which was a genuine 18-line byte-identical duplication. Tests: 32 green.

Second walk-back of the de-duplication pass, scoped to this ticket's files only. REMOVED as ceremony: the makeDataset() call passed a background colour that withStaticSeriesColors() then immediately overwrote (a redundant argument I had introduced); the nested double-call is now one staticColourDataset() helper. RESTORED after breaking a test: sharedUniqueRangeMemoKey() — I inlined it having counted call sites in app/ ONLY, and missed that the regression test proving the cross-widget fetch-collapse seeds that exact key. A reader and a writer that must agree on a key format is exactly when a method earns its keep. Also fixed a stale docblock reference to the renamed colour helper. Tests: 32 filtered, 86 dashboard widgets, 217 pages.

findings_fixed: HIGH (all 3 lanes) — getSharedUniqueHitStatsForRange() called HitPlateStatsBatchQuery::handleRange() bare. VERIFIED: that path bypasses ClickhouseQuery::query() entirely, so nothing swallows in ANY env, and query() itself only swallows in production|testing. The total sibling HAS a guard, so a CH blip degraded the total to zeros while the unique path threw -> a real production 500 on Company Metrics. Driver's own Phase-4 instruction ('a catch there is dead code') caused this. Fixed by mirroring the sibling guard exactly; the incorrect docblock was replaced with the real reason.

HIGH (claude1 M1 / claude2 M-1 / claude3) — Carbon::createFromFormat('Y-m', ...) inherits today's day-of-month, so on a 31st a 30-day target month overflows and ->startOfMonth() cannot undo it. Driver-proved: today=2026-08-31, '2026-06' -> 2026-07-01. The batch window shifted, result keys missed, and the write loop cached 0 for a real month under a ONE-YEAR TTL across all four widgets. Fixed in BOTH the new unique path AND the pre-existing total path via a shared monthKeyStart() helper anchored on 'Y-m-d'.

HIGH (claude2 H-2 / claude3) — resolvePastUniqueMonths() persisted fabricated zeros for a year when the batch query returned [] (exactly what a swallowed production failure returns). Fixed: an entirely-empty result now skips all cache writes AND skips the completion guard so a later request retries; a single month legitimately absent from a non-empty result still caches 0, which is a real answer.
LOW (claude3 M3) — added explicit `_peerdb_is_deleted = 0` alongside FINAL per okf/concepts/clickhouse-query-patterns.md:75. Provable no-op here (native is-deleted engine arg); test counts unchanged.

CI-BREAKER (2 lanes, round 3) — a round-3 test hardcoded ClickHouse port 18123 to 'restore a live connection'. VERIFIED CI runs ClickHouse on 8123 (.github/workflows/lint_check_and_test.yml:30, deploy.yml:43), so in CI that restore was a no-op and the follow-up assertion passed for the WRONG reason, proving the opposite of its comment. Fixed by capturing the original connection config and restoring that — environment-agnostic. 17 passed.

MEDIUM (2 lanes, round 3) — 4x query amplification + ineffective negative marker. ROOT CAUSE (diagnosed empirically, not assumed): PHP gives EACH class that `use`s a trait its own copy of the trait's static properties, so `static::$sharedUniqueRangeStats` was four independent per-class arrays across LiveHits/HistoricalHits/StagingLiveHits/StagingHistoricalHits — never one shared memo. Fixed by layering a genuinely cross-class store (Laravel's cache(), one Cache Manager regardless of caller class) in front of the per-class static, re-keying the failure marker to drop the widget prefix (with a scope param so past-months and range markers don't collide), and giving the range path the negative cache it never had.

HIGH (claude1 H-2, round 4) — three new tests executed real ClickHouse SQL with NO RequiresClickhouse guard. VERIFIED under a proper pgsql-bridge config: 3 hard failures. Fixed with a per-test requireRealClickhouse() guard (the class cannot use the trait wholesale — most of its tests are cache-only and must keep running under the bridge). Now: bridge = 3 skipped + only a PRE-EXISTING unrelated failure ('chart widgets keep the vendor view...', not one of this ticket's tests); real CH = 21 passed.
findings_residual: HIGH (claude1, round 3) — the fabricated-zeros-under-a-long-TTL defect class is repaired only on the NEW unique path; three sibling sites remain live: SharedHitStatsData:121-138 (total past-months, one-year TTL), :153-159 (total current-month, 10-min TTL), and ScanCount:117-131 (one-year TTL). claude1's scope argument is sharp and fair: this commit ALREADY edits ScanCount to fix the sibling month-overflow, so 'different tile, out of scope' is no longer available as a defence. Fixing these is a refactor of the dashboard caching layer, materially larger than DEV-2406.

MEDIUM (2 lanes, round 3) — currentPeriodUnique() issues four identical hits_cold FINAL scans per render on today/last_7d (once per hit widget); the sibling total method uses a shared fan-out. The negative-cache marker is keyed per widget PREFIX, so it does not prevent the 4x amplification its own docblock says it prevents, and the range path has no negative cache at all. This IS a defect in code this ticket adds.
